sections.text: Beyond lies the Path, from which, when found, there is no return. This is the Primal God from whence this ancient creation has sprung.

The wise attain Eternity when, freed from pride and delusion, they have conquered their love for the things of sense; when, renouncing desire and fixing their gaze on the Self, they have ceased to be tossed to and fro by the opposing sensations, like pleasure and pain.
न तद्भासयते सूर्यो न शशाङ्को न पावकः।
Neither sun, moon, nor fire shines there. Those who go thither never come back. For, O Arjuna, that is my Celestial Home!

We had been discussing chapter 15. We have seen in last two chapters the nature of Prakriti. Chapter 15 is Purushottami Yoga, Yoga of the Supreme Purusha. So now we are learning about the nature of Purusha. So the chapter begins with explaining the tree of Sansar. That Sansar which I find it very real and that which I consider is the real reality is explained in the first three verses.
So its a Urdhvamoolaha Adashakaha. The allegory used is of a tree because it exponentially growing. Just like a tree grows over a period of time. So this tree of my Sansar is growing exponentially. But its real picture given here is Urdhvamoolaha. The source of this tree is up above and the branches are below and the leaves are below.
This tree of Sansar is growing in this world with the branches spreading all over. The more I know about this Sansar, the more this tree grows. The more I know about things and beings, the more my Sansaar grows -- networking more people. The more people I know, the more my network grows. The more people I have relationships with.
My network grows in this world. The Veda -- the knowledge -- increases my Sansaar, and as my Sansaar increases, I start developing roots, not knowing what my real source is, because the source is unavailable for me to see. So I develop roots here. The more actions and experiences I have, the more roots grow here. So the actions are creating new channels in this world and then establishing me in this Sansar.
I start thinking this is where I come from. I cannot find my real source. So I consider this Sansar as my source. So my roots are now growing in this world. And Bhagavan said that Naarupam Ashya iha Tatha Upalambita. Its overall form is not available to me.
I cannot figure out how this Sansaar started and how I got entangled into it. Naantah Nachadhi Nacha Samprateshta. I cannot figure out where it started, where its going to end, and how it is rooted in this world. Asvattam Enam Suvirudamulam -- if you want to know the overall picture, we have learned before: one who knows both, he is the Veda Vida. One who knows the source and the Sansaar.
One who knows the Purusha and Prakriti together is the Veda Vit -- he is the knower of the Vedas. We know only part of it, like the Karmakanda, the actions. What we do in this world, we are aware of it, but we consider ourselves to be Gnani. But one says thats only partial knowledge. Thats what is actually binding me to this world.
Because I dont have complete knowledge. Veda describes both the Purusha and Prakriti. Therefore one who knows both is the Veda Vida. To become a Veda knower, you have to go beyond this perception of Prakriti. Only with the weapon of non-attachment can I understand what is binding me to this world.
What will release me from this world and give me the overall picture is detachment. Therefore, with that weapon of detachment, firmly cut this tree. Tathaha Padam Tat Parim ar Gita Vyam Yasmin Gadhana Nivardanti Bhuyah. This statement comes over and over again in our scriptures. Tasmin Gada na Navaratanti Bhuyaha. One who goes there, he never comes back.
Because this life is just one small part of our existence. Our existence is infinite. It started when the world started and will continue till the world ends. This life is just a small sliver of my existence. So Im trying to resolve all my issues during this lifetime.
But you say it will be nothing but a continuation. End of this life will not be the end of anything. End of the life will be just a milestone. Move on to the next mile. But if I really want to resolve all that I want to resolve in this life, I need to go to a place where I dont have to come back again and again to resolve my issues. My issues are Im trying to avoid unhappiness.
Im trying to go beyond sorrows. He said that can only happen if you go to a place where there are no sorrows or where there is no mortality. That place, that goal should be sought. Right now Im seeking goals which are temporarily giving me happiness. My accomplishments, my acquirements, all these things are giving me happiness, but temporarily. So he said, if you want to go there, then you have to seek that goal.
Now what is that goal? Tamevacha Adhyam Purusam Prapadyam Yat Pravrutvicha, Prasuta Purani. Then now I seek refuge in that primeval Purusha, that original source from which stream forth all the ancient activity. The real source of this activity, the Sansar, is the Purusha. Unless Im conscious about my Jagat, my Jagat does not exist. Unless you are conscious, your Jagat, your Jagat does not exist.
This world exists as it is because we are aware of it. Bhagavan said from that source, the consciousness is the source from which all the activity started. My Jagat comes into being as soon as I become aware of it. If Im not aware of it, it does not exist for me. So Bhagavan said that seek that place from which all the activities started, that consciousness. So he said, now my goal is that I seek refuge in that primeval Purusha from which all the activities have started.
So we have defined the goal. We have defined the Sansar. The Sansar seem like roots are here. As we say, wherever we settle down, we form our roots. So now that Im in Richmond, my roots are in Richmond. I have forgotten all about my previous roots.
People come from Northern Virginia. I dont have time for them. I come from India, but I go back and I feel uncomfortable there. All your formative years in your life were here. And suddenly you feel uncomfortable because you are detached from those roots. The things which we used to find so common, we can find anymore because we keep changing where we establish ourselves.
But once you establish yourself into your original source source, then you will not have to move around. We establish the goal that I need to take refuge in that primeval Purusha, the original source. And my original source, as I know is, everything that I know is because Im aware of it. My consciousness is the source of all my experiences. My entire Jagat exists because Im conscious. So I want to take refuge in that.
So then the next verse gives us the qualifications to be achieved -- or, when will I be able to achieve that state? It says: nirmana moha, jita sangha dosha, adhyatma nitya, vinivratta kamah, dvandvaihi vimuktaha, sukha dukha sangaihi gacchanti amudhaha padam avyayam tat. The six qualifications given here are something similar to what we have learned before, all throughout the Bhagavad Gita. And we have concluded already: not possible. We right away said, this is not possible for us. So we move on to the next chapter.
So first is Nirmana Moha -- the one who is free from pride and delusion. Mana and Moha: both relate to my assessment of my situation, and typically my assessment is overly liberal about myself. So Bhagavan said, Moha -- that over-assessment of myself -- creates the delusion about my importance. Once I have the correct assessment of myself, then I will not have the delusion. So Mana, my importance -- I can say, without me the world cannot function, my company cannot function.
I dont know what will happen if Im not there tomorrow. This society cannot function unless I do this. That wrong perception that I am so important creates the situation which makes me unhappy. In the end all this impurities because of the attachment. My attachment creates the false perception. As we said, the people we like, no matter what they do, its okay.
The same event if you watch on Fox News will be completely different than if you watch on MSNBC. The country is divided into two: those who watch Fox News and those who watch MSNBC. This is because of Sangha -- attachment. That attachment creates dosha, a false perception of reality. So maybe you have to watch CNN instead.
So it is my attachment which is creating false perception which is creating dosha in my perception. Therefore Jita Sanga Dosha 1 is victorious over attachment and the stain which comes with it. Adhatma nityaha established in the self. Our mind obviously have to have something to attach to. Our mind cannot stay without any object to think about. Mind does not exist if you dont think about anything.
Therefore, in deep sleep there is no mind because there are no objects. In my deep sleep, I dont exist. In deep sleep, the world does not exist. The mind does not exist in deep sleep. As soon as I wake up, the mind rises because all the things which I associate with come into its perception -- my house, my car, my family, my work, my job.
Very first moment in the mind is active. So all this talk about jita sangha do saha I say not going to happen. Because more I try to avoid attachment, I get attached more. So Bhagavan said then you have to create an attachment which is so powerful that no other attachment can touch you. That attachment with your own self Adhyatmanity. Constantly remembering that Im not this body, not this mind, not this intellect.
These are my equipment. This world is temporary but myself is permanent. That constant churning in your mind will give you the ability to detach from Other things. So adhyatma nitya -- then you are free from desires. My memory bank is the root cause of all the problems. Thats why when we see somebody, we dont see him or her as they are right now.
Right now we remember everything. Our encounter with that person in the past. If the memory bank said the encounter was good, the person is good. The memory encounter wasnt that pleasant. The person is not good. So this memory bank creates ideas and then it creates a desire and the mind starts longing for it.
If we stop power of this memory bank to guide our perceptions, Bhagwanji will see things as they are. If I can judge a person from the day Im looking at him it will be very different than all the baggage of all my experiences with him before. If you judge him from what he does today then it will be a very different perception. Even the person who is a big criminal. But once he resolved to be good, he should be considered good. Because he should be judged on what hes doing today not what he has done in the past.
But we obviously cannot function that way. We have to find all his resume, what he did in the past, and then only can we judge people. Bhagavan said, vinivrutta kamaha -- if you dont do that, there wont be any desire to do anything which is not appropriate. Dvandvai vimuktaha -- we have learned this over and over again. It is the most difficult concept to understand: being beyond pairs of opposites.
That does not mean the pairs of opposites go away. Pairs of opposites remain as they are. Sukha du kha mana apman they all remain exactly where they are. Winter and summer all those things remain. But I become indifferent to them. Thats a dvandvai hi vimuktaha.
Just like in the last chapter we have learned what is the first quality of a guna titaha. Hes a Gunatidha one he does not despise when the gunas are present. Also he does not long for them and they are not present when Tamas is there and despise and seek sattva. But I take them as they are and not get attached to them. So therefore he said dhvandvayihi vimukta he is not affected by one or the other.

These verses reveal both the destination and the qualifications needed to reach it. Yasmin gata na nivartanti bhuyah - having gone there, one never returns. This is not a place in space but a state of being where the cycle of seeking, finding, losing, and seeking again finally ends. The primeval Purusha from which all activity has sprung forth is described as the ultimate refuge. Today, notice how much of your energy goes into seeking temporary refuges - in accomplishments, relationships, entertainment - only to find yourself seeking again tomorrow. What would it mean to seek refuge in the source itself?
The qualifications listed - freedom from pride and delusion (nirmana-moha), victory over attachment (jita-sanga-dosha), constant abidance in the Self (adhyatma-nitya), freedom from desires (vinivrtta-kamah), and liberation from the pairs of opposites (dvandvair-vimuktah) - may seem impossibly high. But verse six offers hope: that supreme abode is not illumined by sun, moon, or fire, because it is self-luminous. Your own awareness is that light. Practice this: when you feel buffeted by lifes dualities - praise and blame, success and failure - pause and ask: Who is aware of both? Who remains unchanged? That unchanging witness is a doorway to the place from which there is no return.
